title: STAT 110 Final Exam Cheat Sheet — Supported Topics

allowance.rules: Student confirmed one sheet, two sides (2026-11-18); paper size and content/format restrictions are unknown.

blocks.text: **Core question:** “What share of [reference group] also has [outcome]?” Start by naming the reference group; its count is the denominator.

blocks.setup: One table; switch the reference group to see why the two answers differ.

steps.label: Counts
steps.text: Among 40 students: 25 commute; 10 of the commuters cycle.

steps.label: Commuters among cyclists
steps.text: If the table gives a cyclist total, divide the commuter cyclists by that total. This is a different question and usually a different percentage.

blocks.takeaway: P(A | B) means the share in B that is also in A: both A and B / total in B. The group after the bar sets the denominator.

blocks.prompt: A column percentage was requested, but the row total was used.
blocks.first_error: The recorded attempt selected a row total for a column percentage.
blocks.fix: Column percentage = cell / column total. Row percentage = cell / row total. Name the reference group, then use that group's total.
blocks.conditions: Each row of row percentages sums to 100%; each column of column percentages sums to 100%. Percentages down a column need not sum to 100%.

blocks.text: Course reporting rule in the supplied outline: report proportions as percentages to **one decimal place** and name the reference group in words (for example, “40.0% of commuters”).

blocks.setup: A grouped summary calculates one chosen summary, such as a mean, for each non-empty category.

steps.label: Summarize
steps.text: Calculate the mean score separately within each section.

steps.label: Output size
steps.text: Four non-empty sections produce four rows, whether the original data had 120 students or another number.

blocks.takeaway: Compare like with like: mean with mean, count with count. A group mean is not a group total.

blocks.text: Bayes’ rule is listed in the outline, but its teaching notes are not posted. Get the lecture notes before relying on a rule or formula for this topic.
